summary: The screened recent arXiv window is strongest on jet-medium response and non-equilibrium QGP dynamics, with an EKT-derived equilibrating parton shower, a kinetic-theory proposal for imaging non-hydrodynamic modes through jet-wake angular moments, and fRG-plus-hydrodynamics net-proton cumulants for Beam Energy Scan critical-point phenomenology. Light-ion structure remains active through alpha-cluster constraints from O+O and Ne+Ne flow, while LHCb adds a forward pp/pPb average-pT measurement that favors hydrodynamic calculations over saturation-only descriptions in the reported comparison. The most transferable AI/ML work concerns non-Abelian neural quantum states with dynamical fermions, reduced-order-model double-descent diagnostics, physics-informed kernel theory, and conformal adaptive sensing.
strongest_paper: 2607.26143: An Equilibrating Parton Shower for Jet Quenching and Medium Response
top_takeaway: The most scientifically important theme is the effort to connect microscopic jet evolution, equilibration, and measurable medium response in a common kinetic-theory language; the most practical AI/ML theme is uncertainty- and physics-structured surrogate modeling rather than generic model substitution.

papers.title: An Equilibrating Parton Shower for Jet Quenching and Medium Response
papers.abstract: The authors derive a parton shower from QCD effective kinetic theory that reproduces the full linearized Boltzmann equation, combining elastic and inelastic collisions so hard-parton energy loss and thermal equilibration are handled consistently. The framework connects jet evolution to hydrodynamic response including wakes, Mach cones, and multiparticle correlations.

papers.title: Imaging non-hydrodynamic modes with jet wakes
papers.authors_short: Aleksi Kurkela, Ian Moult, Alexander Soloviev, Urs Achim Wiedemann
papers.abstract: The paper proposes the angular structure of jet wakes as a probe of non-hydrodynamic QGP modes. In the long-wavelength limit, hydrodynamics contributes only to the lowest angular moments while higher moments encode microscopic non-equilibrium relaxation spectra in a kinetic-theory framework.

papers.title: Critical net-proton number fluctuations with hydrodynamics
papers.authors_short: Rui-zhe Zhao, Shi Yin, Shanjin Wu, Lipei Du, Xiaofeng Luo, Wei-jie Fu
papers.abstract: The paper computes net-proton cumulant ratios C2/C1, C3/C2, and C4/C2 on hydrodynamic freeze-out hypersurfaces at nine collision energies from 7.7 to 200 GeV. It includes fRG-derived regular and critical fluctuations, experimental pT and rapidity acceptances, isospin randomization, global baryon conservation, and noncritical baselines.

papers.title: Constraining alpha-cluster compactness in 16O and 20Ne at TeV energies using azimuthal anisotropy
papers.authors_short: Aswathy Menon Kavumpadikkal Radhakrishnan, Suraj Prasad, Neelkamal Mallick, Raghunath Sahoo, Gergely Gabor Barnafoldi
papers.abstract: Using IP-Glasma+MUSIC+iSS+UrQMD, the paper simulates O+O and Ne+Ne at 5.36 TeV with Woods-Saxon and alpha-clustered configurations and varies cluster compactness. It compares v2{2} in ALICE, CMS, and ATLAS acceptances with Run 3 measurements and reports sensitivity especially in O+O centrality trends.

papers.title: Measurement of the average transverse momentum of forward prompt charged particles in pp and pPb collisions at sqrt(sNN)=5.02 TeV
papers.authors_short: LHCb Collaboration: R. Aaij, M. Abdelfatah, A.S.W. Abdelmotteleb, C. Abellan Beteta, F. Abudinen, et al.
papers.abstract: LHCb presents first measurements of forward prompt charged-particle average transverse momentum versus collision multiplicity and pseudorapidity in pp and pPb at 5.02 TeV. The abstract reports decreasing average pT with pseudorapidity, most pronounced in high-multiplicity events, and states that 3+1D hydrodynamic calculations reproduce the data while saturation models are incompatible.

papers.title: Neural quantum states for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories with dynamical fermions
papers.authors_short: Gabriel Rouxinol, Julian Bender, Michele Grossi, Patrick Emonts, Jad C. Halimeh
papers.abstract: The paper presents a variational Monte Carlo framework for fully continuous SU(2) lattice gauge theory with dynamical staggered fermions, using a neural gauge wavefunction and gauge-covariant Gaussian fermionic correction. It validates against strong-coupling perturbation theory and maps a coarse phase diagram for L=4,6,8.

papers.title: Origins and mitigation of double descent in reduced order modeling
papers.authors_short: Andrei A. Klishin, J. Nathan Kutz, Krithika Manohar
papers.abstract: The authors develop a Data-Noise Averaging theory for double descent in sparse sensing and reduced-order reconstruction, predicting risk curves cheaply, identifying unstable sensors and combinations, and providing regularization mechanisms. Demonstrations include sea-surface temperature reconstruction and time integration of a PDE reduced-order model.

papers.title: PIKS: Universal Physics-Informed Kernel Methods
papers.authors_short: Joachim Bona-Pellissier, Giacomo Meanti, Matteo Santacesaria, Lorenzo Rosasco
papers.abstract: PIKS introduces physics-informed kernel estimators for linear differential constraints, proving universal consistency for universal kernels and deriving finite-sample bounds under source conditions. Numerical experiments compare with PINNs and finite-element methods.

papers.title: Conformalized Rate-Adaptive Sensing
papers.abstract: CoRAS adaptively selects an acquisition or compression rate for each image while maintaining high-probability reconstruction error control. It calibrates stopping-time estimates using early reconstruction paths and reports target coverage with fewer measurements than fixed-rate baselines.

cautions.title: Rotating mirror with all-directional pinch compressions - The beauty and simplicity in controlled nuclear fusion
cautions.abstract: The abstract proposes a rotating-mirror fusion concept with detached electrodes and radial/longitudinal pinch compression, then extrapolates from existing results to potential Lawson-criterion performance. It is patent-framed and does not indicate direct validation of the complete concept or a quantified uncertainty budget in the abstract.
